hook: Launched in nineteen seventy-seven, Voyager one is still sending messages to Earth from interstellar space.

blocks.narration: Launched in nineteen seventy-seven, Voyager one is still sending messages to Earth from interstellar space. It is almost one light-day away.
blocks.visual: Cinematic 3D render of the Voyager probe drifting in deep black space, a faint Sun far behind, glowing accents

blocks.narration: It launched in September nineteen seventy-seven to fly past Jupiter and Saturn, sending back stunning close-up images of both worlds.
blocks.visual: Voyager swings past the swirling bands of Jupiter, then the golden rings of Saturn

blocks.narration: In nineteen ninety, it turned back and photographed Earth from billions of miles away, a tiny dot Carl Sagan called the pale blue dot.
blocks.visual: A sunbeam crosses a dark frame with a single pale blue speck of light

blocks.narration: In twenty twelve, it became the first human-made object to cross into interstellar space, beyond the Sun's protective bubble.
blocks.visual: Voyager passes through a shimmering boundary where solar wind meets interstellar space

blocks.narration: Today it is more than fifteen billion miles away. A signal from it takes nearly a full day to reach us.
blocks.visual: A slow pulse of light travels from the probe toward a distant Earth as a clock ticks

blocks.narration: It runs on heat from decaying plutonium, and that power fades every year. Engineers keep switching systems off to keep it alive.
blocks.visual: Inside the probe, indicator lights blink off one by one in the darkness

blocks.narration: It also carries a golden record with sounds and images of Earth, a message for anyone who might one day find it.
blocks.visual: The golden record glints in starlight, engraved symbols catching the glow

blocks.narration: It is humanity's farthest traveler, and it is still out there, still listening. Follow for more space stories that feel like science fiction.
blocks.visual: Voyager drifts away into a starfield as the camera slowly pulls back

cta: Follow for more space stories that feel like science fiction.

captions.hook_line: Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 is still talking to us from interstellar space 🛰️
captions.body: Voyager 1 launched in 1977, crossed into interstellar space in 2012 and is now more than 15 billion miles away, approaching one light-day from Earth. Its plutonium power supply weakens each year, so engineers keep switching systems off.

youtube_title: Voyager 1 Is Almost One Light-Day From Earth
